content: 1. Administer terbinafine at a dose of 5 mg/day orally for 6 weeks in patients aged 4 years or older weighing more than 35 kg. Increase the dose to 250 mg/day orally for 6 weeks if necessary. No results are available for this regimen. 2. Terbinafine increases the levels or effects of intranasal metoclopramide by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative drugs. Adjusting the dose of intranasal metoclopramide is not feasible when used with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. 3. Terbinafine decreases the levels or effects of pacritinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative drugs. 4. Terbinafine reduces the efficacy of Saccharomyces boulardii through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative drugs. Systemic or oral antifungals may reduce the activity of probiotics. 5. Terbinafine increases the levels or effects of topical sofpironium by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative drugs. Co-administration with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors may elevate sofpironium levels and increase the risk of adverse effects. 6. Amiodarone increases the levels or effects of terbinafine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7.
